plan: Given it's round 1 of 1, and I don't have prior bidding history, I'll assume opponents bid somewhat randomly. To maximize profit, I want to win if my value exceeds the second-highest bid. I'll bid slightly above what I estimate the average opponent bid to be, but below my value. I estimate the average value to be around $25, so I'll bid $22. This minimizes the risk of overpaying while still offering a good chance to win.

Given it's a single round, and my value is $18, I need to balance winning with avoiding overpaying. Assuming others bid somewhat rationally, I expect bids to be scattered. A bid slightly above the midpoint of possible values ($24.5) seems reasonable to increase my chances of winning without excessive cost. I'll bid $18.10 to try and win at my value.

Given my value is $25, I need to bid high enough to win against likely bids, but not so high that I overpay. Since this is round 1 and there's no history, I'll assume the other bidders will bid somewhat randomly. A conservative approach is to bid slightly above the midpoint of possible values. I will bid $17.50. This aims to win against bids likely below $17.50, while still leaving a profit margin if I win.
